Onchain Derivatives Protocol Variational Raises $110 Million at a $1.5 Billion Valuation According to Bloomberg, Cayman Islands-based onchain derivatives protocol Variational raised $110 million at a $1.5 billion valuation in a round led by Bain Capital Crypto, with participation from Dragonfly Capital, HSG and Peak XV. Variational offers perpetual futures and swaps tied to cryptocurrencies, stocks, commodities and pre-IPO shares of companies such as OpenAI. Operating as a broker, it routes orders to crypto protocols and centralized trading firms. Variational had previously raised approximately $61.8 million, including a $50 million Series A round led by Dragonfly in May 2026. — link

CoinShares, Europe’s Largest Digital Asset Manager, Sells All Treasury ETH and Half Its SOL to Support Share Buyback Plan of Up to $40 Million In its third-quarter 2026 earnings report released on November 18, CoinShares disclosed that it sold all of its treasury ETH, worth $16.6 million, and 50% of its SOL, worth $2.7 million. The sales freed up $19.3 million to support a share buyback plan of up to $40 million. Third-quarter net profit was $39.58 million, reversing the previous quarter’s loss and rising 27% year over year. Revenue fell 44.9% year over year to $27.69 million. Assets under management recovered to $7.4 billion at the end of September, with quarterly net inflows of $125 million. — link

October 2026 Exchange Derivatives Volume Report: total $3.75 trillion, MoM increased 3.7%, futures/spot ratio 6.01x; Deribit rose 5x after consolidating with Coinbase WuBlockchain data show that derivatives trading volume across 11 major exchanges reached $3.75 trillion in October 2026, up 3.7% month over month. Binance led with $1.79 trillion (47.8% market share), followed by OKX at $652.3 billion (17.4%) and Bybit at $381.6 billion (10.2%). Deribit recorded the largest increase, surging 507% to $192.1 billion, mainly driven by its integration with Coinbase International Exchange and a sharp rise in USDC-settled perpetuals and futures trading. The futures-to-spot trading volume ratio climbed 14.4% to 6.01x, compared with 5.26x in September. — link
